description: Die MBW Marketing- und Absatzförderungsgesellschaft für Agrar- und Forstprodukte aus Baden-Württemberg mbH (MBW) ist eine Gesellschaft des Landes Baden-Württemberg. Aufgabe der MBW ist es, den Absatz von Agrar- und Forstprodukten aus Baden-Württemberg zu fördern und damit die Marktchancen der heimischen Land- und Ernährungswirtschaft nachhaltig zu stärken. Hierzu setzt die MBW insbesondere Maßnahmen und Projekte in den Bereichen Marketing und Absatzförderung, Messen und Veranstaltungen sowie Presse- und Öffentlichkeitsarbeit um. Die MBW entwickelt und realisiert Marketing- und Absatzförderungskonzepte und unterstützt Kooperationen entlang der Wertschöpfungskette. Zu ihren Tätigkeiten gehören insbesondere gemeinschaftliche Verkaufsförderungs- und Kommunikationsmaßnahmen, die Beteiligung an Fach- und Verbrauchermessen sowie die Konzeption und Umsetzung von Werbe- und Öffentlichkeitsmaßnahmen. Darüber hinaus wirkt die MBW an der Umsetzung und Weiterentwicklung der Qualitätsprogramme des Landes Baden-Württemberg sowie an den damit verbundenen Maßnahmen der Qualitätssicherung mit. Die MBW dient außerdem als Informations- und Kooperationsnetzwerk und arbeitet hierzu insbesondere mit Akteuren aus Landwirtschaft, Ernährungswirtschaft, Handel, Tourismus und Gastronomie zusammen. Detaillierte Informationen rund um das Gemeinschaftsmarketing Baden-Württemberg finden Sie auf der Webseite www.gemeinschaftsmarketing-bw.de und www.schmeck-den-süden.de. Im Rahmen des offenen Verfahrens sucht die MBW eine leistungsfähige und erfahrene Agentur zur strategischen, konzeptionellen und operativen Unterstützung ihrer Informations-, Kommunikations- und Marketingmaßnahmen. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist es, eine Agentur auszuwählen, die die MBW bei der Umsetzung und Weiterentwicklung bestehender Kommunikationsmaßnahmen sowie bei der Entwicklung und Umsetzung neuer Formate und Maßnahmen unterstützt. Dabei soll künftig insbesondere auch die digitale Kommunikation und die Weiterentwicklung der Social-Media-Aktivitäten der MBW einen stärkeren Stellenwert einnehmen. Die MBW setzt im Auftrag des Ministeriums für Ländlichen Raum, Landwirtschaft und Heimat Baden-Württemberg (MLR) verschiedene Maßnahmen zur Kommunikation und Vermarktung von Landesprogrammen und -marken um. Hierzu zählen insbesondere das Qualitätszeichen Baden-Württemberg (QZBW), das Biozeichen Baden-Württemberg (BIOZBW) sowie weitere Maßnahmen und Projekte des baden-württembergischen Gemeinschaftsmarketings. Dabei soll künftig insbesondere auch die digitale Kommunikation und die Weiterentwicklung der Social-Media-Aktivitäten der MBW einen stärkeren Stellenwert einnehmen. Die MBW setzt im Auftrag des Ministeriums für Ländlichen Raum, Landwirtschaft und Heimat Baden-Württemberg (MLR) verschiedene Maßnahmen zur Kommunikation und Vermarktung von Landesprogrammen und -marken um. description: Limited to firms on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). This solicitation of offer is limited to offerors registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). The Contractor will perform all work from its own facilities. No travel is anticipated for the duration of the resulting contract. In executing the work, Contractor managed devices, tools and IT services will only be used when processing unprotected information. The OAG will provide a laptop computer and access to the OAG network when the work requires access to protected information. Term The period of the Contract is from 1-April-2027 to 31-March-2029 inclusive, with the option to extend the Contract for up to two (2) additional two-year periods.

title: Finland – Software package and information systems – Crypto Asset Tax Calculation Solution
description: Crypto Asset Tax Calculation Solution The Finnish Tax Administration seeks to procure a production-ready software solution for the processing, analysis and tax calculation of crypto-asset transaction data. The purpose of the procurement is to support tax assessment, tax control, tax audits and analytical activities related to crypto-assets. The solution will be used to analyse cryptocurrency transaction histories, determine the tax consequences of crypto-asset transactions and produce information that can be further utilised within the Finnish Tax Administration’s internal processes and systems. The procurement concerns a software solution capable of importing, processing, analysing and exporting cryptocurrency transaction data originating from multiple sources. Such data may be obtained from taxpayers, cryptocurrency exchanges and trading platforms, cryptocurrency wallet applications, blockchain addresses and other sources of cryptocurrency transaction information. The solution is intended to support the Finnish Tax Administration in the examination of cryptocurrency transaction histories, identification and classification of transactions, reconstruction of transaction chains, identification of transfers between wallets and service providers, calculation of capital gains and capital losses, and application of cryptocurrency tax rules. In addition, the solution shall support the export of transaction and calculation data for further processing within the Finnish Tax Administration. The solution may be used both as a standalone tool for cryptocurrency transaction analysis and tax calculations and as a source of transaction and calculation data for use within the Finnish Tax Administration’s internal systems. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction Project NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000003, located in Dutchess, Nassau, Suffolk and Saratoga Counties, New York; Sullivan County, New Hampshire; and Hampden County, Massachusetts. The project consists of bridge maintenance and pavement preservation of roadways and parking areas across several parks including Home of FDR National Historic Site (HOFR), Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (ELRO), Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site (VAMA), Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS), Saint Gaudens National Historic Park (SAGA), Sagamore Hill National Historic Park (SAHI), Saratoga National Historical Park (SARA) and Springfield Armory National Historical Park (SPAR). The work includes thin lift asphalt overlay, chip seal, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, pavement markings, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 29, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. title: Poland – System and support services – Usługa asysty technicznej narzędzia CMS wraz z jego rozbudową
description: 1. Przedmiotem zamówienia jest Usługa asysty technicznej narzędzia CMS wraz z jego rozbudową. Zamówienie obejmuje następujące działania: 1) Działanie I – obejmuje świadczenie asysty technicznej posiadanego przez Zamawiającego CMS polegające na: a) Usuwaniu błędów zaistniałych w CMS posiadanym przez Zamawiającego wraz z jego wszystkimi funkcjonalnościami, w tym poprawną integracją z posiadanym przez Zamawiającego systemem WOWZA Streaming Engine. Zapewnienie stabilności, bezpieczeństwa, spójności rozwiązania dla sześciu (6) instancji CMS (objętych asystą). b) Wsparciu pracowników Zamawiającego w zakresie obsługi i działania posiadanego CMS oraz istniejących serwisów (maksymalnie 50 zapytań / miesiąc dla wszystkich istniejących instancji objętych asystą oraz serwisów). 2) Działanie II (z Prawem opcji) – obejmuje rozbudowę i modyfikację CMS oraz istniejących serwisów opartych na narzędziu CMS (modyfikacja funkcjonalności, nowe funkcjonalności) w ramach roboczogodzin programistycznych: a) Zamawiający przewiduje w ramach Działania II maksymalnie 350 roboczogodzin, w tym: - 110 roboczogodzin jako zamówienie podstawowe, - 240 roboczogodzin jako zamówienie opcjonalne, w całym okresie trwania Umowy z tym, że jest to wartość maksymalna i z zastrzeżeniem lit. b. b) Zamawiający zastrzega sobie Prawo Opcji do Działania II. Zamawiający wskazuje, że z uwagi na okoliczności techniczne, organizacyjne roboczogodziny mogą zostać wykorzystane w mniejszym wymiarze, tj. w wymiarze zamówienia podstawowego czyli 110 roboczogodzin. W przypadku nie skorzystania przez Zamawiającego z prawa zlecenia rozbudowy i modyfikacji CMS w wymiarze większym niż 110 roboczogodzin, Wykonawca nie będzie wnosił żadnych roszczeń z tego tytułu. 2. Spełnianie wymogów WCAG na poziomie wymaganym zgodnie z obowiązującymi przepisami prawa (w tym m.in. Ustawy z dnia 4 kwietnia 2019 r. o dostępności cyfrowej stron internetowych i aplikacji mobilnych podmiotów publicznych, Rozporządzenia Rady Ministrów z dnia 12 kwietnia 2012 r. w sprawie Krajowych Ram Interoperacyjności, minimalnych wymagań dla rejestrów publicznych i wymiany informacji w postaci elektronicznej oraz minimalnych wymagań dla systemów teleinformatycznych, Ustawy z dnia 19 lipca 2019 r. o zapewnianiu dostępności osobom ze szczególnymi potrzebami). 3. Ze względu na specyfikę przedmiotu zamówienia Zamawiający przewiduje obowiązek dokonania przez Wykonawcę sprawdzenia dokumentów niezbędnych do realizacji zamówienia, udostępnionych w siedzibie Zamawiającego, zgodnie z zapisami pkt VIII Opisu przedmiotu zamówienia (OPZ) stanowiącego Załącznik nr 3 do SWZ. Niedochowanie powyższego obowiązku będzie skutkować odrzuceniem oferty na podstawie art. 226 ust.1 pkt 18 ustawy Pzp. 4. Zamawiający uprawniony jest do skorzystania z prawa opcji, o którym mowa w art. 441 ust. 1 ustawy Pzp, na zasadach opisanych w paragrafie 2 i 6 załącznika nr 2 do SWZ -projektowanych postanowieniach umowy (PPU). 5. Opis przedmiotu zamówienia (w skrócie: OPZ) stanowi: Załącznik nr 3 do SWZ / Załącznik nr 1 do projektowanych postanowień umowy. 6. Projektowane postanowienia umowy w sprawie powyższego zamówienia publicznego, które zostaną wprowadzone do treści umowy znajdują się w Załączniku nr 2 do SWZ. 7. Instrukcje dla Wykonawcy znajdują się na Platformie pod adresem: https://slaskie.ezamawiajacy.pl/servlet/HomeServlet?MP_module=main&MP_action=publicFilesList&clientName=slaskie&USER_MENU_HOVER=publicFilesList

title: Belgium – Advertising and marketing services – European Potato Promotion Campaign
description: From 2020 to 2025, VLAM, CNIPT, Bord Bia and Europatat collaborated on the European fresh potato promotion campaign “Potatoes, prepare to be surprised – Europe’s favourite since 1536”. Building on this experience, the four organisations are joining forces for a new three-year information and promotion campaign, co-funded by the European Union. The new campaign offers an opportunity to develop a fresh and distinctive creative concept. While lessons from the previous campaign can serve as inspiration, we expect an original, new approach, without being bound by the branding, slogan or visual identity of the previous campaign. The new campaign wants to stimulate the consumption of fresh potatoes at EU level and more specifically in three countries, i.e. Belgium (Flanders), France and Ireland. Target group of the campaign is people between 25 and 44 years old The communication objective of the new campaign is to highlight the ease of use (convenience) and versatility of fresh potatoes (pleasure) and their place in a contemporary lifestyle and a healthy, balanced and sustainable diet. The campaign activities include a mix of promotional activities, some implemented in all target countries, others in 1 or more target countries. Common activities include the design of a common look & feel, website, social media template and video. Local activities include collaboration with influencers and creation of local social media posts and/or videos. Our target group will be reached via a multi-channel approach, with a focus on video and social media advertising in all countries. This approach will be extended with native advertising in Flanders and Ireland and PR activities in France.

The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.** *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30th, 2026 as of 10:30am ET. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/artificial-intelligence-ai-decision-making-process-visibility-traceability-and-compliance-governance Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) Funding Mechanism: Contract MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE: Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. Phase 2: • The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. • The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report). • Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: No travel required. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice. The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices. Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight. Details: Essential (mandatory) Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required. 2. Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization. 2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks). 2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms. 2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments. 3. Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements. 3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention. 4. Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities. 4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital, Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act. 4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user. 4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. description: Objets des services du marché : DEVELOPPEMENT DE PROGRAMMES ET DE MODULES DE FORMATION EN E-LEARNING DANS LES THEMATIQUES DES MARCHES PUBLICS ET DE L’ORGANISATION FINANCIERE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. Le marché public est divisé en lots. Les soumissionnaires sont libres d’introduire une offre pour un ou pour plusieurs lots. L’ensemble des lots organisés par le présent marché visent à l’élaboration, la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement, la livraison, l’intégration avec support technique dans la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP ainsi que la maintenance de trois modules de formation/apprentissage au format e-learning, disponibles simultanément en versions française et néerlandaise. Les lots 1, 2 et 3 visent l’élaboration de trois programmes d’apprentissage (objectifs, contenus, dispositif pédagogique) rendus disponibles en langue française et destinés à s’intégrer dans des modules en e-learning. Ces 3 programmes portent sur les trois thématiques suivantes : - « Introduction aux achats publics des administrations communales et des CPAS bruxellois ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des administrations communales bruxelloises ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des CPAS bruxellois ». Les lots 4 et 5 visent la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement technique et la maintenance des trois modules de formation au format e-learning sur base des trois programmes d’apprentissage susmentionnés. Hébergement des modules e-learning : les modules de formation e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP (voir description technique en annexe). Le cas échéant, les modules e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS d’un ou plusieurs administrations clientes ou sur un site Internet. Il est à noter que le présent marché ne couvre pas les services liés à l’intégration des modules e-learning sur d’autres plateformes que celle mise à disposition par l’ERAP. Durée des modules e-learning : Les modules de formation au format e-learning visés par les lots 4 et 5 ont une durée respective estimée à 60 minutes (2 x 30 min. ou 4 x 15 min.). Thématique des modules : Ces modules s’intègrent dans un parcours de formation plus large destiné à l’onboarding des agents de niveau A, B ou C des administrations communales et des CPAS de la Région de Bruxelles-capitale. Estimation du nombre d’utilisateurs finaux pour chacun des trois modules d’apprentissage : environ 550 personnes par an (500 apprenants/utilisateurs finaux et 50 responsables représentants les administrations concernées + personnel ERAP). Durée du marché : pour tous les lots, le marché est conclu pour une durée d’un an, renouvelable trois fois pour la même durée, pour une durée totale de 4 ans (voir point II.7 pour les détails). Le marché est divisé en lots de la manière suivante : (1) LOT 1 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (2) LOT 2 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES BRUXELLOISES. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (3) LOT 3 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (4) LOT 4 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DU MODULE E-LEARNING D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES COMMUNES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS (DURÉE ESTIMÉE : 60 MINUTES), EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. (5) LOT 5 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DES DEUX MODULES D’APPRENTISSAGE EN E-LEARNING (CHACUN D’UNE DURÉE ESTIMÉE DE 60 MINUTES) PORTANT RESPECTIVEMENT SUR (1) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES COMMUNES BRUXELLOISES (2) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS, EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. Délais de livraison : Pour les lots 1, 2 et 3 (voir point III.2.6) ; Pour les lots 4 et 5 (voir point III.3.7)

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: France – Public road transport services – DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC RELATIVE A LA GESTION ET L’EXPLOITATIONDES SERVICES DE MOBILITE ET DE TRANSPORT DE VOYAGEURS SUR LETERRITOIRE DE CHATEAUROUX METROPOLE
description: La consultation a pour objet de déléguer la gestion et l’exploitation des services de mobilité et de transport de voyageurs sur le ressort territorial de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole (Réseau Horizon) Châteauroux Métropole, autorité Organisatrice de la mobilité est autorité délégante. Les missions déléguées sont les suivantes: Offre de base : Exploitation et gestion des services de mobilité et de transports publics de personnes et à l’échelle du territoire communautaire selon les principes définis à l’article 5.1 du document programme. Les candidats devront obligatoirement répondre à l’offre de base et à l'option obligatoire.• Option obligatoire :Option N°1 : Exploitation et gestion d’un service de location de vélos L’option est décrite à l’article 5.2 du document programme. L’Autorité Délégante précisera, avant la remise de l'offre finale si l'option est levée. Le Délégataire assurera la gestion de ces services pour une durée de six (6) ans, à compter du 01/01/2028 et jusqu’au 31/12/2033 dans le cadre d’une délégation de service public (DSP) au sein du périmètre contractuel. Lieu d’exécution : Territoire de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole(département de l’Indre). L’estimation de la valeur du contrat de concession est de 45 millions d’euros HT valeur décembre 2026 sur la durée du contrat. Les missions attendues sont l'organisation, la production et la commercialisation des services, ainsi que la réalisation de l'offre de transport et la maintenance des véhicules et outils de production.Le délégataire assurera en outre la gestion de la relation avec les usagers des transports scolaires qui sont assurés par le biais de marchés publics en cours. La future DSP intègre la gestion et l'exploitation des services de transport suivants sur l’ensemble du périmètre de l’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole : • Le réseau de transport en commun « Horizon » composé aujourd’hui de 12 lignes régulières, • Le service de transport adapté à la demande, « Handibus », à destination des personnes à mobilité réduite sur le périmètre de CM .Pour cette gestion déléguée, la collectivité met à la disposition du délégataire : • Un dépôt de bus réceptionné en 2021 avec une capacité de stationnement de 80 véhicules, équipé de bureaux, d’un atelier de maintenance, de stations de lavage et de carburant et d’équipements de recharge de véhicule électrique; • 31 autobus standard, 5 autobus articulé, 2 midibus. Ces véhicules sont équipés d’équipements de suivi par système SAEIV et cellules de comptage voyageurs. Plusieurs véhicules standard et articulés électriques ont également été commandés. • 2 midibus accessibles et équipés pour accueillir des PMR • Un Site Internet https://www.bushorizon.com/ La présente concession est passée sur le fondement du règlement 1370/2007 et de la directive 2014/23/CEE. La directive 2014/25/UE citée dans le présent avis concerne les marchés des secteurs spéciaux est non les concessions , elle ne s'applique pas à la présente consultation.

The project consists of the reconstruction and addition of new lanes for a continuous four-lane roadway with two lanes in each direction for an approximate distance of 2052 ft. (0.39 mi). The work includes widening and reconstruction of Veterans Drive, enhance pedestrian and vehicular safety, and improve drainage of the roadway and other miscellaneous work. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. title: ATR Plant Protection System (PPS) Seismic Switch Replacement
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the management and operating contractor for the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified suppliers capable of providing environmentally and seismically qualified seismic switches for use in the Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) Plant Protection System (PPS). The purpose of this EOI is to identify suppliers with the technical capability, quality assurance program, testing facilities, and experience necessary to provide safety-related seismic switch equipment qualified for nuclear applications. This EOI is being issued for market research and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to identify potential suppliers for a future procurement opportunity. The EOI process is used by INL to develop a list of qualified and interested vendors that may be considered for future solicitations. BACKGROUND The ATR Plant Protection System currently utilizes seismic switches to provide a critical reactor protection function. Seismic switches detect ground motion and initiate a reactor scram when predetermined seismic thresholds are exceeded. The existing Kinemetrics Model TS-3A seismic switches are obsolete and have demonstrated performance degradation, resulting in increased reliance on limited spare inventory. Additionally, one seismic switch is currently out of service, placing the PPS in a reduced logic configuration. Replacement with modern, supported equipment is required to restore normal system configuration and ensure long-term reliability and maintainability. SCOPE OF INTEREST BEA seeks information from suppliers capable of providing complete seismic switch solutions meeting the functional, environmental, seismic qualification, testing, documentation, and quality assurance requirements typically associated with nuclear safety-related applications. Functional Capability Three-axis ground motion sensing capability. Dry contact output suitable for reactor protection system input. Adjustable seismic trip setpoints. Response times consistent with nuclear protection system applications. Long-term reliability and maintainability. In-situ testing and calibration capabilities. Environmental and Seismic Qualification Respondents should be capable of qualifying equipment consistent with applicable industry standards, including IEEE 603 IEEE 323 IEEE 344 ANSI/ISA-67.04.01 ASME NQA-1 Deliverables Suppliers should be capable of providing: Complete seismic switch assemblies. Required mounting hardware and accessories. Qualification documentation and test reports. Operation and maintenance manuals. Installation and interface documentation. Calibration and surveillance procedures. Certificates of conformance and applicable certifications. MINIMUM MANDATORY CAPABILITIES To facilitate evaluation, respondents should clearly identify whether they can meet the following minimum capabilities: Provide a seismic switch solution capable of detecting low-level seismic events suitable for reactor protection applications. Demonstrate environmental and seismic qualification in accordance with IEEE 323 and IEEE 344 methodologies. Maintain a Quality Assurance Program consistent with ASME NQA-1 requirements or equivalent controls. Support a qualified service life suitable for long-term nuclear facility operation. Provide qualification reports, testing documentation, calibration information, and supporting quality records. Provide long-term product support, maintenance recommendations, and obsolescence management. RESPONSE FORMAT AND SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested organizations shall submit a concise response demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities, and interest in supporting this requirement. Responses should be limited to approximately 10 pages, excluding product literature, drawings, certifications, and supporting quality documentation. Responses should include, at a minimum: Organization name, mailing address, and primary point of contact UEI and CAGE Code (if applicable) Business size and socio-economic classifications Technical capabilities Relevant experience Quality Assurance Program information Manufacturing and delivery capabilities Estimated lead times Assumptions, exceptions, or recommendations related to the requirement Responses shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to: Chase Egbert & Stacey Hill Email: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov and Stacey.Hill@inl.gov Responses must be received no later than: April 23, 2027 PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents should clearly identify any proprietary or confidential information contained within their submission. DISCLAIMER This Expression of Interest (EOI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or commitment by BEA or INL to procure supplies or services. BEA reserves the right to use information received through this EOI to evaluate market capabilities, acquisition strategies, and potential supplier interest. Submission of an EOI response does not guarantee participation in any future solicitation and does not obligate BEA or INL to award a contract. BEA is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing or submitting responses to this EOI. Information obtained through this process may be used to assist in developing future procurement requirements and solicitation strategies

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND NEXT GENERATION DISTRIBUTED COMMAND AND CONTROL
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. No other changes are made. PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL AMENDMENT DETAILS. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 20 Sep 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 4 Oct 2023 FY25 by 30 Sep 2024 FY26 by 30 Sep 2025 FY27 by 30 Sep 2026 FY28 by 30 Sep 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. title: Netherlands, Germany – Industry specific software development services – Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program (Dynamic Purchasing System - EU-404)
description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to determine the availability of vendors that can provide a Utilization Management Software Tool with VHA enterprise-wide licensing that includes unlimited use, updates, and clinical and technical support for evidence-based criteria and the associated tools identified in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) that interface seamlessly into the National Utilization Management Integration (NUMI) application and the Electronic Health Record (EHR). In addition, the Contractor shall provide training to certify and maintain certification for trainers throughout the VHA.. This RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy Product Description (PD) or Performance Work Statement (PWS). Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. BACKGROUND VHA is committed to a healthcare system that treats its patient population effectively, efficiently, and appropriately. The VHA s Utilization Management (UM) Program focuses on using resources efficiently and ensuring that every Veteran receives consistent reliable, high-quality care in the optimal setting and at appropriate care delivery intervals. The objective of the UM program is to provide the correct care, for the right patient, at the best time and for the proper reasons using evidence-based practice and continuous measurement and improvement. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION In response to this RFI, VA seeks to gain industry feedback on the DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS). Please respond with suggested approaches/recommendations to the attached PWS, Vendor Questions, and RFI Respondent Information. Responses should not exceed 10 pages, single-spaced standard 1-inch margins and in a 12-point font. Responses to this RFI shall be submitted via email, with filename - Utilization.Management.rfi-name of your company - to William.Freer@va.gov and debra.clayton2@va.gov no later than December 11, 2026 at 3 PM EDT. VENDOR QUESTIONS Describe your solution s ability to meet all the requirements set forth in the attached Draft PWS. � Please specifically address the following requirements: Ability to Interface with NUMI (do you have this capability out of the box or is time required to develop?) Interface with the Cerner Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) (do you have this capability out of the box or is time required to develop?) Unlimited licenses available of the review products and ease of access for all users Multiple avenues to access the review products- book view, interactive anonymous, application, NUMI, Cerner, Mobile access Training of new VHA instructors each year with vendor verification through certification and relevant continuing education credits, and yearly sustainment training of current instructors with certification and continuing education credits. The opportunity to increase yearly sustainment training if needed. Reporting capability (please include any enhanced reports available) Describe how your system is hosted and how VA users would access the system. � If your solution is cloud-based, please describe your FedRamp certification status. Describe what type of training is provided with your solution and any recommendations related to how a workforce consisting of over a thousand users would be transitioned to your solution. � 2. How would user access be managed for your services and is it possible that specific VA users would be provided a direct ability to grant or remove user access? � � 3. Describe your technical support capabilities and what kind of help desk/customer services your solution provides. � 4. Does your solution utilize any form of Artificial Intelligence, Process Automation or other functions to enhance functionality? � 5. Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimate to include pricing models that would be most advantageous to the Government. � � 5. Describe your pricing methodology. Is there a price per user unit price? Do you offer an enterprise license? Do you offer tiered pricing methodology? � Do you offer the ability to choose different products, vice all included ? � RFI RESPONDENT INFORMATION Vendors shall provide the following information: Name of Company Address Point of Contact Phone Number Email address CAGE Unique Entity Identifier Number Company Business Size and Status for NAICS NAICS code(s) applicable to the products and services you can provide Any contract vehicle of which you are part that can be used to acquire your products/services. Typical contract vehicles include General Services Administration contracts, National Aeronautics and Space Administration Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement VI, or other Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts. Please also include Contract Number, expiration date, and point of contact. Socioeconomic data: If a small business, what type of small business are you? Are you able to comply with federal acquisition regulations clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting in execution of this effort? Are you able to comply with 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction and with subcontracting limitations in accordance with 13 CFR 125.6 in execution of this effort? This information will assist in determining whether a set aside may be appropriate for this effort. As part of market research, after RFI responses are received and reviewed, VA may contact you for additional information.
