buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – General management consultancy services – 10035189-Advice on implementation of AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol and technical inputs to related reforms; facilitation and development of partnerships with the private sector on digital trade
description: The project "Pan-African e-Commerce Initiative 3 - Boosting African Digital Trade" (PeCI 3) is a regional technical cooperation project implemented by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) in the context of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The project aims to strengthen an enabling environment for cross-border digital trade in Africa, with a particular focus on micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women-led businesses. PeCI 3 contributes to the BMZ"s core area "Sustainable Economic Development, Training and Employment" and supports it"s digital policy and Africa Strategy through the promotion of inclusive digital trade ecosystems, and public-private cooperation. The project builds on the achievements and partnerships established under the previous phases (PeCI 1 and PeCI 2). Earlier phases supported MSMEs in adopting e-commerce solutions and digital sales channels, strengthened intermediary organisations providing training and advisory services, facilitated public-private exchange on digital trade issues and contributed to regional approaches related to e-commerce, digital payments, consumer protection and electronic transactions. The project also strengthened cooperation with the East African Community (EAC), the Smart Africa Alliance (SAA) and the AfCFTA Secretariat. PeCI 3 supports implementation of the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol (DTP), adopted by the African Union in 2024, by strengthening structures, processes and cooperation mechanisms required for cross-border digital trade. The project addresses barriers affecting MSME participation in digital trade, including fragmented regulatory frameworks, limited interoperability of digital payment systems, logistics and last-mile delivery challenges, gaps in online consumer protection and limited coordination between public and private actors. Particular attention is given to barriers affecting women"s participation in digital trade ecosystems. The project operates at pan-African, regional and national levels and combines technical advisory services, stakeholder consultations, public-private dialogue formats and capacity development measures. Activities include support for implementation of selected DTP chapters, facilitation of cross-border exchange on best practices, development of cooperation models between private-sector actors and intermediary organisations, and support for gender-sensitive approaches to digital entrepreneurship and MSME support services. Environmental sustainability is integrated as a cross-cutting topic, including approaches related to sustainable packaging and resource-efficient logistics. The project is implemented in cooperation with public, private and regional stakeholders in selected AfCFTA countries, particularly Ghana and Kenya, as well as with the EAC. Lead executing agencies are the Ministry of Finance in Ghana, the Ministry of Investments, Trade and Industry (MITI) in Kenya and the EAC Secretariat. Additional partners include the AfCFTA Secretariat, the Smart Africa Secretariat, chambers of commerce, business and e-commerce associations, payment service providers, logistics companies, innovation hubs and women"s business networks. PeCI 3 further aims to strengthen cooperation between African, German and European private-sector actors to promote cross-border digital trade and MSME participation. The project cooperates with business associations, e-commerce platforms, logistics and payment providers, chambers of commerce and innovation actors, including bevh, AHKs and African e-commerce associations. Cooperation with UNCTAD, ITC and initiatives supported by the European Union and the World Bank further strengthens synergies and regional outreach. The project is scheduled to run until June 2028.

title: High-Altitude Platform System (HAPS) for Ultra-Long-Range (ULR) Wireless Backhaul
description: ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.*** This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/high-altitude-platform-system-ultra-long-range-wireless-backhaul The Department of National Defence (DND), Shared Services Canada (SSC) and National Research Council of Canada (NRC) are seeking the development of a solution that will extend the reach of ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e. over-the-horizon ranges) using High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS). Challenge sponsor: National Research Council (NRC) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date : October 20, 2026 Closing date : December 1, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Problem statement The Government of Canada recognizes the critical role that advanced communication technologies play in supporting national defence, public safety, and the security of Canadians. Reliable and resilient connectivity in dangerous, remote, and sparsely populated regions is essential for effective defence operations, emergency response, and border monitoring. However, delivering such connectivity remains a significant challenge due to Canada’s vast geography, low population densities, and extreme environmental conditions. The Department of National Defence, Shared Services Canada and National Research Council of Canada are seeking the development of a solution that leverages High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to provide ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e., over-the-horizon ranges). This capability will enhance communications under harsh weather or challenging terrain in theatres of conflict, in remote areas, and isolated regions with little to no current connectivity. The ultimate goal is to improve secure, high-speed communications for Canadian defence, surveillance, and emergency operations while also potentially benefiting civilian emergency response connectivity needs. The successful applicant is responsible for securing a demonstration site as well as a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC) clearance from Transport Canada to demonstrate the HAPS capabilities. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Demonstrate the capability to travel from the surface up to 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers and travel laterally within the corridor of 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers. 2. Operate at a specified, nominal, fixed point relative to the Earth for an extended period (minimum of 3 days). 3. Launch, deploy, and operate from land or water-based environments. 4. Provide a minimum of 100 Watts to support the deployment of long-range sensors. 5. Deliver high-bandwidth, high-availability, ultra-low latency wireless connectivity comparable to current offerings (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) in the telecommunications industry. 6. Support current (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) wireless systems and infrastructure. 7. Provide a minimum of 1000 km² service area coverage and a minimum of 200 km² of transit area coverage based on usage demands. 8. Be deployable within 6 hours for heavier-than-air HAPS or within 24 hours for lighter-than-air HAPS. 9. Incorporate automated decision-making for flight maneuvers and operations. 10. Operate at cold temperatures between -50 to at least -70 degrees Celsius. Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Have a power management system that optimizes power consumption and adapts to usage demand. 2. Be capable of continuous power generation and recharging during ground operations and flight through renewable energy sources. 3. Have non-assisted launch and land capability from land or water-based environments. 4. Support next generation wireless systems and infrastructure. 5. Maintain wireless connectivity in the presence of intentional and unintentional wireless channel interference. 6. Provide communications link security features and platform hardening to prevent signal interception, hacking and unauthorized platform hijacking. 7. Demonstrate the ability to daisy chain the signal using intra-HAPS (i.e HAPS group 1 to HAPS group2), and/or inter-HAPS (between individual HAPS). 8. Support backhauling requirements for future wireless networks. 9. Complement the terrestrial communication infrastructures. 10. Minimize the amount of traditional backhaul hopping. 11. Support point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, and mesh links. Background and context High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) are unmanned vehicles designed to operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 20 to 50 kilometers above the Earth's surface. HAPS are classified into two main types: Lighter-than-air (LTA) platforms and Heavier-than-air (HTA) platforms. LTA platforms include balloons and airships characterized by low energy consumption but has limited maneuverability. On the other hand, HTA platforms which include light unmanned aircrafts that rely on electric motors to generate and maintain lift offer greater maneuverability but have payload weight restrictions and can have an energy deficit issue as a result of prolonged dark periods during winter months at higher latitudes. HAPS offer several advantages such as its ability to be airborne for long durations and less expensive to operate compared to satellites. Since HAPS fly at lower altitudes than satellites, they are able to provide low latency data communications. The propulsion systems for HAPS generally use sustainable energy sources which have a lower environmental impact than rocket launches for satellites. Presently, existing wireless backhaul technologies have limitations in terms of coverage and during emergency situations for remote areas, nomadic users, and scattered populations. A merging solution between HAPS and ULR (Ultra-Long-Range) wireless backhaul, offering broadband services, would be a great benefit to a wide range of populations, especially in times of crisis and during emergency situations where traditional telecommunication services suffer outages. Additionally, HAPS are highly effective platforms for enhancing military communications and remote sensing capabilities. They can be used to complement military satcom infrastructure, offering capabilities in intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. When equipped with high-resolution cameras, radars, and signals intelligence systems (SIGINT), HAPS provide continuous coverage of areas of interest. title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). SECTION 2 � GUIDELINES FOR SOLUTION BRIEFS, PITCHES, AND PROPOSALS 2.1 The purpose of the Solution Brief is to identify innovative solutions and preclude effort on the part of the Company whose proposed work may not be of interest to the Government. Companies are encouraged to follow the instructions detailed below. The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. The original of each submission received will be retained by USSOCOM and all other non-required copies destroyed. 2.3 Guidelines for Solution Brief Submissions: 2.3.1 It is generally desired that active Research and Development (R&D) and technology application is underway for potential solutions submitted under this CSO. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] and each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: �

title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) PEO-SDA
description: SAM.GOV Special Notice Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) H9241525X0001 US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) PEO SOF Digital Applications (SDA) SECTION 1 � INTRODUCTION 1.1 USSOCOM Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics (SOF AT&L) seeks to accelerate the application of commercially derived software innovation into deployable warfighting capabilities in support of Special Operations Forces (SOF). Early identification of warfighter needs and continuous engagement with users during software development and fielding will support increased lethality and efficiency. 1.2 In order to support rapid fielding of tailored software capabilities, SOF AT&L seeks to award FAR and non-FAR contracts and agreements to non-traditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects for Program Executive Office SOF Digital Applications (PEO SDA) that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of software intensive programs, platforms, components, algorithms, and processes. As such, under the authority of 10 USC � 3458 and DoD Class Deviation 2022-O0007, USSOCOM SOF AT&L releases this Commercial Solutions Opening. This CSO may result in an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) or a FAR-based contract. 1.3 This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will make awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2024 and 2025. Awards may include prototypes as well as concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile software development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. Interested vendors should note that all of PEO SDA�s Programs of Record are being managed in accordance with DoDI 5000.87, the software acquisition pathway, for the timely acquisition of custom software capabilities developed for the DoD. Programs will require government and contractor software teams to use modern iterative software development methodologies (e.g., agile or lean), modern tools and techniques (e.g., development, security, and operations (DevSecOps)), and human-centered design processes to iteratively deliver software to meet the users� priority needs. 1.3.1 Phase I: Solutions will be sought on a full-and-open basis under certain Technology Areas of Interest (AOI) relevant to SDA requirements. Initial submissions against 2024 and 2025 AOIs will be requested as Solution Briefs (SB). A team of Government personnel who are subject matter experts for the given AOI will evaluate each submission independently against standard criteria for advancement to Phase II. The Government may elect to proceed directly to Phase III after a successful Phase I evaluation. 1.3.2 Phase II: If a Phase II evaluation is necessary, the Government will host Phase II invitees so that each company has a standard amount of time to pitch / demonstrate its proposed solution to the Government evaluation panel and hold any discussions necessary for evaluation. Discussions may continue outside of the pitch / demonstration session. Participation in Phase II will be entirely at the company�s expense. Favorably evaluated pitches will receive a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) that marks the beginning of Phase III. Note, Phase II is optional for the CSO process, and may not always be conducted, or may not be required for every successful Phase I submission. 1.3.3 Phase III: The Government will only advance companies to Phase III if it intends to award a contract or agreement for the proposed solution. Companies will collaboratively build Statements of Work with the Government team and negotiate Contract/Agreement Terms and Conditions for award. 1.4 Technology Areas of Interest (AOI): Specific AOIs will be posted and advertised intermittently when the Government has particular interest in a further defined problem set for software-intensive capabilities. Technology AOIs will only be posted for a specified amount of time wherein submissions will be accepted. Additionally, specific AOIs will usually have funding set-aside and available to immediately make awards for favorably evaluated proposals determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Examples of future AOIs are as follows but not limited to: The development of Software Lifecycle Management tools, Software Process Improvement/Education, Automation Tooling for Data Ingestion/Tagging, and innovating novel approaches to Machine Learning (ML) Ops processing. 1.5 This notice fulfills synopsis requirements. Synopsis under FAR subpart 5.2 of the individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO is not required. All Technology AOIs will be publicized at https://www.sofwerx.org. Announcements of individual contract actions for AOIs under this CSO made at the SOFWERX website are considered to satisfy reasonable efforts to obtain competition in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022 (b)(2). The Government aims to provide an evaluation response NLT the specified evaluation completion date after the submission against specific AOIs. 2.2 Submissions will not be returned. Active R&D includes analytical studies and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology, as well as software engineering and development. Technology application in this case refers to a variety of methods to validate dissimilar capabilities that may be modified to meet a need. 2.3.2 Costs of preparing and submitting solution briefs are at the Company�s expense. 2.3.3 Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. 2.3.4 An overview diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. 2.3.5 Multiple solution briefs addressing different technology AOIs may be submitted by the same organization; however, each solution brief may only address one solution based on the specific AOI. 2.3.6 The period of performance for any solution brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24 months. 2.3.7 Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. 2.3.8 All solution briefs shall be unclassified. Solution briefs containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: �This solution brief includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to contractor support services personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. title: Germany – Translation services – Ausschreibung „Rahmenvereinbarung Übersetzung juristischer Fachtexte („Agenturvertrag“)
description: Das BfJ beabsichtigt, eine Rahmenvereinbarung für die Dauer von vier Jahren mit einer Übersetzungsagentur zu schließen. Gegenstand der Rahmenvereinbarung soll die Übersetzung vorwiegend von juristischen Fachtexten sowie vereinzelt von Texten aus anderen Fachgebieten, die im Rahmen der Zuständigkeiten und Tätigkeiten des Bundesamts für Justiz (BfJ) anfallen, aus sämtlichen Sprachen der Welt ins Deutsche und aus dem Deutschen in sämtliche Sprachen der Welt sein. Im Rahmen der Zuständigkeiten und Tätigkeiten des BfJ besteht ein erheblicher Übersetzungsbedarf. Dieser ist geprägt durch ein Massengeschäft mit einer hohen Zahl von Kleinst- und Kleinaufträgen, die in zahlreichen Sprachen anfallen. Um die große Bandbreite der benötigten sprachmittlerischen Leistungen abdecken zu können, verfügt das BfJ über einen hauseigenen Sprachendienst. Dieser fertigt Übersetzungen teilweise selbst, teilweise vergibt er Übersetzungsaufträge an externe Sprachdienstleister. In den erfahrungsgemäß häufig benötigten Sprachen erfolgt die Vergabe grundsätzlich an freiberufliche Übersetzer/innen. Zur Deckung des verbleibenden, oft schwer vorhersehbaren Übersetzungsbedarfs arbeitet der Sprachendienst darüber hinaus mit einer Übersetzungsagentur zusammen, die alle Sprachen aus einer Hand bedient. Weitere Informationen zur Leistung sind der beigefügten Leistungsbeschreibung (LB) zu entnehmen.

title: Facet Coater
description: For over two decades, the Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre (CPFC) at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) has operated as a mission-critical facility supporting Canada’s photonics and semiconductor innovation ecosystem. The CPFC provides advanced fabrication and metrology services for both internal research programs and external clients, enabling the development and production of cutting-edge photonic devices used in telecommunications, sensing, and quantum technologies. Photonic devices are critical pieces of hardware for high-performance computing in various innovative fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), data centres, automotive LiDARs (Light Detection and Ranging), biomedical, aerospace; security, and quantum industry/applications. The global market for compound semiconductor foundry services is growing rapidly, presenting niche opportunities and challenges for Canada. Limited access to compound semiconductor foundry services poses several challenges to develop, successfully introduce, and supply new products in an increasingly competitive marketplace. Photonic devices fabricated on InP wafers must undergo several “back-end” steps before dicing and packaging, adding time and cost if the assembled parts are then found to be defective. This project will establish the capability at CPFC to deliver known good die (KGD) to clients, to reduce time and cost for new product introduction (NPI). To provide KGD, a new clean room (ISO 6) will be constructed (retrofit of a current facility) to house numerous automated tools, such as Dual Ion Beam Sputter Deposition (DIBS) Laser Facet Coating Systems. This project will address an immediate client need for timely introduction of new products into a competitive marketplace.

description: This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) Task Area to be eligible for a Base ID/IQ contract award. The anticipated period of performance shall not exceed 60 months for the ID/IQ contracts. The main objective of this contract is to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. This requirement demands comprehensive technical expertise spanning pavement, bridge, and other highway infrastructure engineering, as well as advanced data systems: Specifically, the LPES contract vehicle is structured to achieve the following overarching strategic objectives: Execute comprehensive pavement condition data collection, incorporating high-speed 3D surface condition profiling (3D APCS), continuous traffic-speed deflection testing, under a rigorous Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP) to ensure defensible and research-grade data quality. Formulate strategic pavement research plans advancing the LTPP program, conduct targeted performance case studies, and deliver practical engineering tools, Section 508-compliant publications, and technical webinars. Develop and curate specialized, analysis-ready datasets for machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling across LTPP and broader highway infrastructure domains, integrating modern database architectures and coordinating data schemas with web portal contractors for public release. To fulfill the LTPP program mission and support broader FHWA pavement and other infrastructure research, the scope of work is organized across three (3) primary Task Areas. Contractors are not required to perform across all Task Areas unless awarded task orders in those areas: Task Area A � Data Collection and Processing: The Contractor shall provide all labor, contractor-owned survey vehicles, specialized diagnostic equipment, materials, and traffic control services necessary to perform automated high-speed 3D surface condition profiling, as well as deflection testing using the Traffic-Speed Deflection Device (TSDD) and Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) methods. Work also includes executing a comprehensive Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP), performing ground-truth equipment calibrations, field validations, and routine sensor verifications, conducting relational database processing, and delivering verified data for public portal ingestion. Task Area B � Pavement Performance Data Analysis and Product Development: The Contractor shall perform pavement research analytics, review and execute strategic pavement data analysis plans, conduct targeted pavement performance case studies, and advance and validate state-of-the art pavement testing technologies. Work also includes developing user-friendly web-based engineering tools for State DOT practitioners, publishing 508-compliant documents and facilitating regional practitioner workshops for technology transfer. Task Area C � Special Research Datasets Development: The Contractor shall develop, update, and curate specialized research datasets for broader highway infrastructure research applications. Work includes establishing automated ingestion pipelines and designing modern database schemas to process, quality-check, and store high-resolution 3D Automated Pavement Condition Survey (3D APCS) and continuous deflection datasets; engineering and refining automated data pipelines to produce clean, reliable, and optimized datasets, machine learning feature stores, and structured data environments to support advanced computational modeling across FHWA InfoHighway platforms; generating, validating, developing, and updating computed parameters required for mechanistic-empirical pavement design and machine learning models; and executing close technical coordination with external InfoHighway web portal support contractors (responsible for web portal administration and hosting) to align data schemas, resolve technical issues, provide technical support to data users and stakeholders, and ensure seamless dataset delivery for public releases and web portal data deployments.

title: 8910 - Dairy Products and Refrigerated Delivery � VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Dairy Products and Refrigerated Delivery � VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office West (RPOW), Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 5, Health Service Area (HSA) 5.2, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21, on behalf of VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System (VASNHCS), is conducting market research to identify businesses capable of supplying and delivering fresh dairy products for Veteran patient meal services. DESCRIPTION OF ANTICIPATED REQUIREMENT The contractor would furnish the products, labor, refrigerated transportation, delivery equipment, and associated resources necessary to supply and deliver pasteurized milk and other dairy products to the facility located at 975 Kirman Avenue, Building 1C, Reno, NV 89502 at least twice a week. The requirement is defined by product characteristics, freshness, food safety, and delivery performance, rather than a particular brand, manufacturer, or distributor. The prospective contractor would provide the following descriptions and estimated annual quantities: Item 1: Pasteurized 2% reduced-fat milk; half-gallon container; reference pack 12 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 1,000 containers. Item 2: Pasteurized whole milk; half-pint (8-fluid-ounce) individual container; reference pack 70 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 9,500 containers. Item 3: Pasteurized 1% lowfat milk; half-pint (8-fluid-ounce) individual container; reference pack 70 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 43,000 containers. DELIVERY AND QUALITY EXPECTATIONS Anticipated deliveries are twice weekly, Tuesday and Friday, between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. local Reno time, to the address above. Holiday adjustments would be coordinated in advance. Deliveries would include contractor unloading and movement to the designated receiving point in the presence of authorized VA personnel. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT STRUCTURE The Government anticipates an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) supply contract with firm-fixed unit prices and delivery orders issued as needs arise. A 12-month base ordering period and four 12-month option ordering periods are contemplated, subject to confirmation. Contract dates, minimum guarantee, maximum quantity or value, order limitations, and final award structure have not been established and will be stated in any resulting solicitation. Award is anticipated on or about December 20, 2026 and will be made in accordance with the evaluation criteria stated in the solicitation. The Government anticipates issuing the solicitation on or about 12/15/2026. The solicitation will be available for download from https://sam.gov/content/opportunities. Interested vendors are responsible for monitoring that site for the solicitation and any amendments. This acquisition is subject to the Buy American Act (BAA). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 311511, Fluid Milk Manufacturing. The Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard is 1,150 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 8910, Dairy Foods and Eggs. No set-aside determination has been made at this time. The Government is seeking information to support acquisition planning and any applicable socioeconomic determination. REQUESTED CAPABILITY INFORMATION Interested firms should submit a concise capability statement that includes: Company name. UEI and CAGE code. Point of contact name, title, email address, and phone number. Business size under NAICS 311511 and Socioeconomic status, if any. Relevant experience of past performance that demonstrate specific cold-chain logistics, food safety compliance, and reliable delivering/providing dairy products. Identify whether your firm is a manufacturer/processor, distributor, or reseller. Proposed use of subcontractors. Available contract vehicle information, if applicable. Additionally, please answer the following questions (not required): Does your firm intend to submit a bid or quotation if VA issues a solicitation? What lead time is required from award notification to start work and to deliver supplies? What customary commercial practices apply to these supplies and services (explain effects on availability, pricing, and competition)? What additional details would be helpful in submitting your quote? Responses shall be submitted by 12/2/2026 via email to derek.brown7@va.gov. The subject line should include: PRE-SOL RESPONSE � 36C26127Q0182 - Dairy Products and Refrigerated Delivery. This notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. Responses will be considered by the Government; however, a determination by the Government not to complete the proposed acquisition based upon responses of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Design-Build-to-Budget � Fort McCoy Indoor Multipurpose Athletic Facility - Army Combat Fitness Testing
description: DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR27RA005. This project will utilize a Design-Build-to-Budget delivery method to provide a new Soldier Fitness Training and Testing Facility to contain a 54,600 SF multipurpose athletic field via an enclosed structure at Fort McCoy, WI. The Design-Build Contractor shall design and construct the multipurpose facility housing the athletic field to result in a complete and usable facility including all permitting, sitework, and utilities. The facility will consist of an indoor 200-meter rubberized running track and turf infield sized according to Army Techniques Publication (ATP) 7-22.01 Holistic Health and Fitness Training requirements for completing the annual Army Combat Fitness Testing (ACFT). The 200-meter rubberized track will consist of three 4-foot lanes with the lanes striped. Once this project is completed it will be recognized as a permanent facility on Fort McCoy. Supporting facilities include site development, modification to existing improvements, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, sidewalks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Consistent temperature control inside the facility shall be provided by self-contained systems. ATFP measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Antiterrorism for Buildings will be provided. A life safety analysis of the facility shall be conducted to determine compliance with UFC, IBC, and NFPA codes and standards. A new addressable fire alarm system shall be installed in the facility that is compatible with the existing base fire alarm reporting system. Comprehensive building design services shall be required. Accessibility for individuals with disabilities shall be required. The multipurpose athletic facility will be periodically occupied and shall require adequate clearance and circulation for personnel, maintenance and operations. This is not a continuously used facility, and during periods of non-use utilities will be reduced or disconnected to conserve energy. The facility shall be designed to a minimum life of 40 years and in accordance with DoD�s Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated systems performance. Contract duration is currently estimated at 730 calendar days. Funds are not presently available for this acquisition. No contract award will be made until appropriated funds are made available. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be an Unrestricted (Full and Open) Procurement. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design-Build to Budget procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) source selection process. The technical information contained in each offeror's proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. title: Jacksonville Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for Jacksonville Harbor. Jacksonville Harbor: The Jacksonville Harbor, FL - FY27 O and M Contract (non-fed sponsor Jacksonville Port Authority (JAXPORT)) for maintenance dredging typically requires hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s) depending on work location in the~ 20-mile federal channel. The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -47 ft MLLW (w/additional depths for required advanced maintenance areas and allowable over depths) and to transport the dredged sediment to both a designated Dredged Material Placement Area (DMPA) known as Bartram Island and the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS) located approximately 6 nautical miles offshore. Dredged material shall be placed upland in Bartram Island Cell F and the Jacksonville ODMDS Release Zone C1 depending on the specific reach to be dredged. The transport distance to the designated placement areas varies significantly, ranging from direct, local placement to a few miles for the upland placement area and up to 6 miles for ocean disposal from the tip of the south jetty. The work is divided into a base and five options. The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within ten (10) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use not later than 220 days after the Contractor receives the notice to proceed. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. Base: 120 calendar days. Option A: 15 calendar days. Option B: 20 calendar days. Option C: 30 calendar days. Option D: 25 calendar days. Option E: 10 calendar days. Complete all work within Cut-17 Sta. 0+00 through Cut-41 Sta. 20+00 (BASE work), which are located within an Outstanding Florida Waters (OFW), no later than May 20, 2027.This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 02 November 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. description: Project Title: Tactical Communication Systems Procurement, Services & Sustainment (TCS-PSS) Reference Number: CSO-ARMY-TCS-PSS-2027 Primary NAICS: 334220 � Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing 1. Opportunity Overview The Department of the Army, representing the Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN), the Project Manager Command and Control Transport (PM C2T), and the Product Manager Tactical Communication Systems (PdM TCS), has issued a Call for Solutions (CfS) under Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Part 212.70 to establish a 10-year enterprise acquisition framework for innovative tactical communication capabilities. This initiative seeks to secure a mix of single-award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts and/or Other Transactions (OTs) to streamline the procurement, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of both legacy systems and emerging transport hardware and software. Focused on supporting Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2), the effort aims to deliver highly secure�National Security Agency (NSA) High Assurance certified or Sensitive but Unclassified - Encrypted (SBU-E) qualified�resilient, and interoperable communication systems. To counter future cryptographic threats, the framework is seeking capable vendors to provide a plan for incorporating Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) compliant algorithms and achieving National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) validation by 31 December 2030, ensuring robust data protection and mission command resilience in contested joint and coalition environments. 2. Critical Milestones & How to Respond Questions & Comments Due: 04 November 2026 at 16:00 EST White Papers Due: 03 December 2026 at 17:00 EST 3. Points of Contact Contracting Officer: Jennifer Anderson, jennifer.d.anderson57.civ@army.mil Contract Specialist: Aaliyah Coles, aaliyah.m.coles.civ@army.mil Please refer to the attached Call for Solutions (CSO-ARMY-TCS-PSS-2027) document for full submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and detailed technical characteristics. Amendment 2 (26 October 2026) � The submission schedule for the TCS-PSS Call for Solutions has been revised. The deadline for submitting questions is now extended to 04 November 2026, and the submission deadline for White Papers has been extended to 03 December 2026. To reiterate, to request access to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) documents, vendors must complete the following steps: SAM.gov Request: Submit an access request directly through the SAM.gov posting. (Note: ONLY SUBMIT ONE DOCUMENT APPROVAL REQUEST THROUGH SAM.GOV PER VENDOR). Reminder, all vendor questions regarding this CfS must be submitted via the designated Microsoft Forms link. Important: No vendor emails containing questions regarding the CfS will be answered or responded to. The Government will consolidate and provide formal answers to all submitted questions following the final receipt of questions. All other terms, conditions, and submission guidelines remain unchanged. Amendment 1 (19 October 2026; 1600 EST) - The purpose of this amendment is to establish the mandatory security and verification protocols for vendors requesting access to the CUI and Export-Controlled attachments associated with this Call for Solutions. Certain attachments referenced in this Call for Solutions are marked as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) with Limited Dissemination Controls and/or Export Controls. The dissemination of Export-Controlled information is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act or the Export Administration Act of 1979. Export-controlled items shall not be disseminated outside the U.S. Government or to U.S. Government contractors without first verifying the recipient�s eligibility and authority to receive export-controlled information by verifying they have a current, valid DD Form 2345. title: Door Repair IDPO; Defense Supply Center Richmond(DSCR)
description: DUE TO DELAYED PUBLICATION OF THE SOLICITATION THE PREVIOUSLY SCHEDULED SITE VISIT HAS BEEN RESCHEDULED FOR 12/03/2026 at 0930. The new projected date of publication for the solicitation is on or around 11/19/26. The SOW is being revised and will be published with the full solicitation SF1449. This is notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity and site visit. The site visit which was originally scheduled for 11/19/2026 at 0930 has been tentatively rescheduled for 12/03/2026 at 0930. Interested parties MUST follow instructions below in order to gain access to DSCR; it is a secure facility and access is permitted ONLY to those who have been vetted and approved. NOTE: This contracting opportunity is for door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The resultant contract will be an Indefinite Delivery Purchase Order(IDPO). This notice is being published at this time in order to allow adequate time for vetting of persons interested in attending the upcomming site visit. In order to attend the site visit interested parties MUST follow the instructions below no less than 5 business days prior to the site visit. This is to allow time for vetting by base security. Plan on arriving at DSCR an hour prior to the site visit time, as the processing time through the visitor center fluctuates. Follow the link below to register through DBIDS, and a QR code should be provided for each visitor. The QR codes MUST be emailed to the Project Manager, Mike O'Connor <Michael.OConnor@dla.mil> (Work Cell: 804-306-5273). The QR code MUST be emailed to the project manager as soon as possible due to the lengthy vetting process of approximately 5 business days. The project manager will also serve as the sponsor for site visit attendees. A new system was implemented on 3 January 2023 to screen visitors and contractors for installation access at DSCR.The new system is designed to increase efficiencies, enhance the protection of personal information during the vetting process and eliminate the use of hard copy DLA Form 1815s. The new screening system will require visitors and contractors to pre-enroll in DBIDS (Defense Biometric Identification System). To begin the process, visitors and contractors will complete registration through the pre-enrollment website: https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil. Upon entry of their information, visiting personnel will be provided an electronic form to download, which will have an individualized barcode and alpha numeric code. The codes need to be sent to the visiting person�s sponsor(Mike O'Connor). Once in receipt of the barcode, the sponsor will email Security and Emergency Services and provide the barcode and sponsorship information. Once the visitor/contractor is vetted and approved for installation access, Security & Emergency Services will notify the sponsor that the visitor/contractor can go to the DSCR Visitor Center to obtain his/her pass. At the Visitor Center, the visitor provides the barcode and code provided earlier in the process and completes the credentialing process. See attached SOW for full requirement details. Parties interested in this project are advised and expected to have reviewed the entire SOW prior to site visit attendance. This notice of an upcomming contracting opportunity which will be awarded as an indefinite delivery purchase order(IDPO) for door repair service at Defense Supply Center Richmond. The full solicitation will be published on, or around, 11/19/2026 and will remain open for a period not less than 30 days. A site visit will be held on 12/03/2026 at 0930. See map on p.49 of the attached Statement of Work(SOW) for the meeting location for the site visit.

description: InnoPA: Supporting e-Government and Innovation in the Public Administration Supporting eGovernment and Innovation in Public Administration (InnoPA) is a joint project implemented by the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) in Egypt, on behalf of the German Federal Government, and in partnership with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT). The project aims to strengthen the capacities of the public sector and civil society to drive an inclusive and responsive digital transformation in line with European standards. The InnoPA project implements a variety of interventions in the areas of institutional capacity building, innovation promotion, digital inclusion, and policy support. The project adopts the principle of "leave no one behind" to ensure that all segments of society benefit from the digital transformation process and enjoy an effective and responsive public administration. The project has three pillars: 1) Support an inclusive, citizen-centered digital transformation of the public sector, the project aims to bridge the digital divide and increase the uptake of existing digital public services. To this end, collaborations with civil society organizations will be carried out to enhance the digital skills of both citizens and civil servants, alongside additional measures focused on strengthening institutional capacity. 2) promotes innovative solutions for the inclusive and citizen-oriented digital transformation of the public sector. title: FACILITY RENTAL, SUPPLIES AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT SERVICES
description: Notice No.: 75N98027Q00118 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), intends to award a purchase order to the Marine Biological Laboratory (MBL), Woods Hole, Massachusetts, for facility rental, supplies, and technical support services supporting the NINDS Division of Intramural Research, Molecular Neurophysiology Section�s Squid Research Program. Description of the Requirement NINDS requires an integrated combination of specialized laboratory facilities, marine specimen collection and holding infrastructure, live Atlantic longfin squid (Doryteuthis pealeii), laboratory supplies, and technical support services. These resources support research into the biophysical mechanisms governing electrical signaling and membrane fusion in nervous systems. Research activities include electrophysiological, molecular, and morphological studies of squid giant axons and associated neural tissues, including investigation of the potential role of the squid HAP2 homolog, DpHAP2, in neural membrane fusion and giant axon development. The requirement depends on timely access to freshly collected, viable specimens and laboratory facilities located near the coastal collection site. Laboratory and Support Facilities The acquisition includes: Two climate-controlled laboratory rooms totaling approximately 560 square feet, configured for squid giant axon and optic lobe electrophysiology and molecular assays. Workstations with tables incorporating cable cutouts for computer-based scientific acquisition systems. At least one adjacent equipment room for each laboratory. Access to centrifuges, balances, chemical fume hoods, ultra-low-temperature freezers, and cold rooms. Marine Infrastructure and Live Specimen Delivery The contractor must provide continuous, temperature-controlled running seawater holding tanks and live squid collection throughout the approximately six-month Atlantic squid season, generally May through October. The requirement includes delivery of requested quantities of live, vigorous Doryteuthis pealeii directly to the NINDS laboratory holding tanks twice weekly, with delivery days scheduled Monday through Saturday. Collection, holding, and delivery operations must preserve specimen viability and support timely access to neural tissue for the required research. Microscopy and Controlled Experimental Facilities The contractor must provide: Preparative microscopy services. Institutional access to specialized electron microscopy facilities, including a Carl Zeiss Microscopy SEM Supra 40 VP field-emission scanning electron microscope. Access to appropriately authorized radioisotope facilities suitable for low-energy radioisotope experiments. Access to cold rooms and chemical fume hoods. Technical, Computing, and Procurement Support The requirement includes on-site technical and computing support to configure and maintain scientific software, integrate laboratory instrumentation into scientific acquisition networks, support data servers, and maintain secure laboratory wireless connectivity. Additional support includes chemical ordering, laboratory consumables and reagents, equipment rental, hazardous material handling, and shipping logistics. The contractor must provide a monthly Excel supply ledger identifying item names, descriptions, manufacturers, catalog numbers, quantities, list and discounted prices, order and receipt dates, and supporting signed receiving documentation. Supply purchases requiring advance Government approval must be processed in accordance with the resulting award. Period and Place of Performance The anticipated period of performance consists of: Base Period: January 1, 2027�December 31, 2027. Option Period 1: January 1, 2028�December 31, 2028. Option Period 2: January 1, 2029�December 31, 2029. The place of performance is Woods Hole, Massachusetts 02543. The Government anticipates making an award before January 1, 2027, to support laboratory reservations, vessel scheduling, and preparation for the spring collection season. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to use the simplified acquisition procedures at FAR 12.201-1. The decision to restrict competition will be documented in accordance with FAR 12.102(a), applicable to acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold when only one source is available. Acquisition.GOV MBL is the proposed source because the requirement depends on an integrated combination of live marine specimen collection, continuous running seawater infrastructure, co-located research laboratories, specialized microscopy, controlled experimental facilities, and scientific technical support. This acquisition involves more than the rental of laboratory space or the purchase of biological specimens. The required research depends on coordinated access to live Atlantic squid and specialized laboratory infrastructure capable of supporting electrophysiological and molecular studies soon after collection. Based on the requiring activity�s technical assessment and market research, commercial specimen suppliers and alternative coastal research facilities have not been identified that can provide the complete combination of live collection capabilities, seawater holding infrastructure, dedicated laboratory space, adjacent equipment rooms, radioisotope facilities, specialized electron microscopy, and technical support required for this work. Obtaining individual elements from separate sources would not, by itself, satisfy the requirement for coordinated collection, specimen holding, and research operations at the coastal laboratory site. Delays or interruptions in access to viable specimens could compromise seasonal tissue collection and ongoing research. The Government therefore proposes to obtain the required facilities, supplies, and services from MBL. The proposed sole-source approach is contingent upon the Government�s determination, based on technical review and market research, that no other responsible source can satisfy all minimum technical and operational requirements. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can satisfy the Government�s requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the complete integrated requirement. Capability statements should include sufficient technical information to demonstrate the firm�s ability to: Provide the required laboratory space, adjacent equipment rooms, and supporting laboratory equipment. Collect and deliver live, vigorous Doryteuthis pealeii twice weekly during the seasonal collection period. Provide continuous, temperature-controlled running seawater holding systems. Provide co-located facilities supporting timely use of viable neural tissue. Provide the specified electron microscopy access and preparative microscopy services. Provide suitable radioisotope facilities, cold rooms, and chemical fume hoods. Provide scientific computing, procurement, hazardous material, shipping, and supply reporting support. Meet the anticipated performance schedule and all other stated minimum technical and operational requirements. The Government will evaluate timely capability statements to determine whether another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. All responsible sources may submit a quotation in response to the subsequent solicitation, which will be considered by the agency. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than December 4, 2026 @ 9:00am est. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00118 in the subject line of the submission.
